chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one in Ihram must not deliberately flick lice from his garment or from his body. If he does one of those things, let him feed food in its place.' I said, 'How much?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'One handful.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a person in Ihram who deliberately flicks lice from their body or clothes?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the penalty of feeding one handful of food applies specifically to the deliberate removal of lice, distinguishing it from accidental removal which incurs no penalty. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of differentiating between intentional acts and natural occurrences during the sacred state of Ihram, ensuring fairness in expiation (kaffarah).
